uncited: Application-Specific Reconstructions refers to the modification of the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) training pipeline to address domain-specific challenges such as dynamic human avatars, displaced objects, or physical plausibility constraints.

While [Base 3DGS Optimization](7549-base-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) provides a generic differentiable rendering loop, this family introduces structural changes—such as physical priors, generative inpainting, or mesh-embedded representations—to handle ambiguities inherent in monocular video or specific geometric constraints.

It sets itself apart from siblings like [WildGaussians](6064-wildgaussians.md) (which handles wild/non-rigid motion via generic deformation) by enforcing explicit domain rules (e.g., canonical space physics or mesh topology) rather than relying solely on learned deformation fields.

The core mechanism shared by all methods in this family is the integration of domain-specific constraints or post-processing steps into the optimization loop defined in [3D Gaussian Splatting Training](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md).
**Constraint Injection:** Unlike vanilla 3DGS which minimizes photometric loss $\mathcal{L}_{photo}$ alone, these methods add regularization terms or structural constraints.
For example, [GaussianBody](9209-gaussianbody.md) adds a physical prior loss $\mathcal{L}_{phys}$, while [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) enforces mesh adherence.

**Representation Modification:** The Gaussian attributes or their initialization are modified to fit the domain. [GauHuman](9198-gauhuman.md) redesigns densification primitives; [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) embeds Gaussians in mesh tangent space with trainable embeddings; [Inpainting for Displaced Objects](9523-inpainting-for-displaced-objects.md) modifies the kernel set by removing and reinitializing specific subsets.

**Specialized Initialization:** Standard SfM initialization is often replaced or augmented. [GaussianBody](9209-gaussianbody.md) initializes in canonical space based on parametric models; [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) initializes one Gaussian per mesh triangle.
**Definition:** A method for defining unknown scatterers in radiative transfer contexts using a grid mapper and extinction transform.
The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting [Kerbl et al., 2023] provides a robust baseline for static scene reconstruction.

However, dynamic scenes, specific geometric constraints, and occlusion handling require specialized adaptations. [GauHuman](9198-gauhuman.md) and [GaussianBody](9209-gaussianbody.md) address the long-standing problem of dynamic human avatars from monocular video, where depth ambiguity leads to artifacts in clothing and body shape. [Inpainting for Displaced Objects](9523-inpainting-for-displaced-objects.md) addresses the specific failure mode of 3DGS when objects move, exposing unseen background. [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) integrates 3DGS with parametric meshes (FLAME) to provide stable, controllable avatars.

These methods represent a shift from generic scene representation to domain-aware reconstruction, leveraging the differentiable nature of 3DGS to incorporate physical, geometric, or generative priors.
